query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing and actionable in these expense records.

per_column.name: amount_tier
per_column.rationale: Bucketing amount into tiers gives a clean grouping axis for expense analysis, distinct enough from raw amount to aid comparison. Values are derivable from the existing amount column, though tier cutoffs are unverifiable from samples (no amount shown); the well-spread distribution suggests a reasonable mapping.

per_column.name: processing_delay_days
per_column.rationale: Delay between opened_at and processed_date is a genuinely actionable operational metric for expense processing. Values are computable from the two date columns; NULLs correctly appear where processed_date is 'nan'. Non-null samples look plausible.

per_column.name: is_pending_or_declined
per_column.rationale: A status flag is useful and actionable for triaging records, though it partly restates the existing 'state' column. Values appear grounded in state/processed_date (flag=1 aligns with missing processed_date in samples), a warranted reading.

per_column.name: high_risk_indicator
per_column.rationale: A risk flag could be actionable, but the derivation is opaque and the values are hard to justify from the shown source text. Rows with similar benign hardware descriptions get differing flags (medium/on-time -> 0 vs low/on-time -> 1) with no visible criterion, suggesting the label asserts risk the text does not clearly support.

judge.rationale: amount_tier and processing_delay_days provide strong, well-grounded new axes for grouping and operational analysis. is_pending_or_declined is useful but somewhat redundant with state, yet still grounded. high_risk_indicator is the weakest: potentially actionable in concept but its values are not transparently warranted by the source text and appear inconsistently assigned. Overall a solid set with one questionable column.
